description: What the router's firewall does with new connections from one zone to another, or to the router itself: rules in order, then a default.

default.description: What happens to a connection no rule matches; `reject` answers with an administratively prohibited error.

rules.description: Rules in order: the first that matches a connection decides.

action.description: What happens to a connection the rule matches; `reject` answers with an administratively prohibited error.

cidrs.description: Address ranges that match; excludes `set`. In each family the rule matches the ranges of that family.

destination.description: Destination addresses: the ranges of an AddressSet in `set`, or address ranges in `cidrs`; null matches every destination.

destinationPorts.description: Destination ports, each a port or a range `<first>-<last>`, with the protocol `tcp`, `udp` or `sctp`; empty matches every port.

family.description: Address family the rule matches; null matches each family its protocol and addresses leave.

icmpTypes.description: ICMP or ICMPv6 types, with the protocol `icmp` or `icmpv6`; empty matches every type. `packet-too-big` is ICMPv6's.

log.description: Whether the kernel logs each packet the rule matches, prefixed with the policy's name and the rule's number.

protocol.description: Protocol the rule matches; null matches every protocol. `icmp` is IPv4's and `icmpv6` IPv6's.

cidrs.description: Address ranges that match; excludes `set`. In each family the rule matches the ranges of that family.

source.description: Source addresses: the ranges of an AddressSet in `set`, or address ranges in `cidrs`; null matches every source.

sourcePorts.description: Source ports, each a port or a range `<first>-<last>`, with the protocol `tcp`, `udp` or `sctp`; empty matches every port.

x-chalkos-rules.description: A rule's source and destination each name an AddressSet or address ranges, one of them.
x-chalkos-rules.message: a rule's source or destination names both set and cidrs, or neither; give one, or leave the field out to match every address
x-chalkos-rules.rule: self.all(r, [r.source, r.destination].all(m, m == null || (m.set == null) != (m.cidrs == null)))

x-chalkos-rules.description: A rule with a family has addresses and sets of that family alone.
x-chalkos-rules.message: a rule has addresses or a set of another family than its own
x-chalkos-rules.rule: self.all(r, r.family == null || (r.source == null || (r.source.set != null ? document("AddressSet", r.source.set).spec.family == r.family : r.source.cidrs == null || r.source.cidrs.all(a, cidr(a).ip(0).family() == r.family))) && (r.destination == null || (r.destination.set != null ? document("AddressSet", r.destination.set).spec.family == r.family : r.destination.cidrs == null || r.destination.cidrs.all(a, cidr(a).ip(0).family() == r.family))))

x-chalkos-rules.description: A rule matches IPv4 or IPv6: its family, protocol, addresses and sets leave one.
x-chalkos-rules.message: a rule matches no connection: its family, protocol, addresses and sets leave neither IPv4 nor IPv6
x-chalkos-rules.rule: self.all(r, ((r.family == null || r.family == "ipv4") && r.protocol != "icmpv6" && (r.source == null || (r.source.set != null ? document("AddressSet", r.source.set).spec.family == "ipv4" : r.source.cidrs == null || r.source.cidrs.exists(a, cidr(a).ip(0).family() == "ipv4"))) && (r.destination == null || (r.destination.set != null ? document("AddressSet", r.destination.set).spec.family == "ipv4" : r.destination.cidrs == null || r.destination.cidrs.exists(a, cidr(a).ip(0).family() == "ipv4")))) || ((r.family == null || r.family == "ipv6") && r.protocol != "icmp" && (r.source == null || (r.source.set != null ? document("AddressSet", r.source.set).spec.family == "ipv6" : r.source.cidrs == null || r.source.cidrs.exists(a, cidr(a).ip(0).family() == "ipv6"))) && (r.destination == null || (r.destination.set != null ? document("AddressSet", r.destination.set).spec.family == "ipv6" : r.destination.cidrs == null || r.destination.cidrs.exists(a, cidr(a).ip(0).family() == "ipv6")))))

x-chalkos-rules.description: Ports go with tcp, udp or sctp, ICMP types with icmp or icmpv6, and packet-too-big with icmpv6.
x-chalkos-rules.message: a rule has ports without the protocol tcp, udp or sctp, or ICMP types its protocol lacks
x-chalkos-rules.rule: self.all(r, (size(r.sourcePorts) == 0 && size(r.destinationPorts) == 0 || r.protocol in ["tcp", "udp", "sctp"]) && (size(r.icmpTypes) == 0 || r.protocol in ["icmp", "icmpv6"]) && !(r.protocol == "icmp" && "packet-too-big" in r.icmpTypes))

to.description: FirewallZone the connections go to, or `local` for connections to the router itself.

title: FirewallPolicy

rules.description: A FirewallPolicy comes from a FirewallZone, not from local.
rules.messageExpression: documents.filter(n, documents[n].spec.from == "local").map(n, "FirewallPolicy " + n).join(", ") + " comes from local, the router itself, whose own connections the firewall accepts; a policy comes from a FirewallZone"

rules.description: One FirewallPolicy at most goes from a zone to another.
rules.messageExpression: cel.bind(pairs, documents.map(n, documents[n].spec.from + " to " + documents[n].spec.to), "more than one FirewallPolicy goes from " + pairs.filter(p, size(pairs.filter(q, q == p)) > 1)[0] + "; give each pair of zones one policy")
rules.rule: cel.bind(pairs, documents.map(n, documents[n].spec.from + " to " + documents[n].spec.to), pairs.all(p, size(pairs.filter(q, q == p)) == 1))
